claim_types.description: Original strategic or conceptual framing used to explain avatar strength, governed representation, or the Avatar Strength Protocol.
claim_types.notes: Must be clearly framed as analysis and not as factual proof.

claim_types.description: A controlled definition of a term used in the StrongAvatar.com reference system.
prohibited_without_source: claiming legal, regulatory, market, or technical authority inside a definition
claim_types.notes: Original definitions may be used, but factual claims inside definitions must follow their claim type.

claim_types.description: A claim about legal rights, obligations, liability, likeness rights, consent, ownership, or legal interpretation.
claim_types.notes: Must include reference-only / not legal advice discipline.

claim_types.description: A claim about regulation, official guidance, enforcement, policy, or formal regulatory requirements.
claim_types.notes: Must use high-trust official or legal-analysis sources.

claim_types.description: A claim about market size, growth, adoption, pricing, traffic, buyer behavior, or category movement.
claim_types.notes: May be framed as strategic analysis only when evidence is not asserted as fact.

claim_types.description: A claim about systems, standards, interoperability, security, APIs, model behavior, or technical capability.
claim_types.notes: Must distinguish observed capability from implementation assumption.

claim_types.description: A claim about what a platform, API, product, avatar system, or identity system can do.
claim_types.notes: Prefer platform documentation or company primary sources.

claim_types.description: A claim about a company, product, policy, pricing, feature, disclosure, or official positioning.
claim_types.notes: Use company primary sources or trusted platform documentation where possible.

claim_types.description: A claim comparing tools, platforms, frameworks, policies, capabilities, or governance approaches.
claim_types.notes: Must be balanced, specific, and source-aware.

claim_types.description: A claim about misuse, harm, impersonation, deepfake risk, abuse resistance, fraud, security, or trust failure.
claim_types.notes: May use explicit analysis framing only when not asserting factual incidence, prevalence, or legal consequence.

claim_types.description: A claim about revenue, paid products, sponsorship, directories, audits, briefs, or commercial activation.
claim_types.notes: Must be supported or framed as internal strategy; monetization remains inactive.

claim_types.description: A claim about acquisition readiness, buyer interest, valuation, strategic fit, or exit potential.
claim_types.notes: Must not make valuation promises and must be framed as strategic posture unless sourced.
